parameters.content:
## Workflow notes
**Double click** to edit me. 
Google OAuth2(recommended) -> go to Google -> Google cloud console -> click on first link to open console.cloud.google.com -> sign in with your gmail and password. New project -> project name -> organisation -> enter Go to left side menu (4 horizontal lines) -> Enabled API & Seevices -> now, we are going to enable 5 x Google related services, starting with - gmail api, Google drive api, Google docs, Google sheets, Google calendar -> enable all the 5 -> you will get enabled notifications. Now go to credentials (from the left side menu)-> create credential->OAuth client ID -> configure consent screen -> Get started. Project Configuration -> 1. App Information -> app name -> dripemaildemo, user support email -> give your organisation email. 2. Audience -> Internal (only for organisations), External (available to any test user) -> Next 3. Contact Information-> email addresses ->give your personal email(or any email you need to get access to) 4. Finish -> I agree to Google API services UDP -> continue -> create -> OAuth configuration created! Metrics -> Create OAuth client -> create OAuth client ID -> application type - web application, name -> dripemailschedulerdemo -> enter OAuth client created -> client ID and client secret. -> copy both and save somewhere -> click ok(from June 2025) won’t be able to change it. Now, we have to establish a connection from n8n -> gmail(Google). In the n8n workflow -> on Gmail node -> send a message -> credentials-> create new credential-> copy the redirect url link -> go to Google console cloud -> click on the OAuth client created name - deipemailscheduler -> go to -> Authorised redirect URIs -> Add URIs -> paste the link here from n8n -> now copy the client ID and client secret and go to n8n workflow -> paste it in client ID and client secret. Go back to google console -> audience -> test user -> add users -> give the email you want to access -> save. Go back to n8n -> inside the gmail node -> connect with Google -> choose the email that you need to connect -> message to say this app not verified -> continue -> hater. Cloud wants to access -> select all -> continue -> n8n - gmail connection successful - YAY - in n8n -> Account connected (green). Now you can fill in -> to address, subject, message -> add options if you want to add attachments, etc. -> execute step -> output -> sent. Check your Gmail inbox -> you would have received the email from the newly created OAuth2 client. This is how you have to do for every other external application to setup OAuth2 - Client ID and Client Secret.
